knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.3.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly distinguishes null vs alternative and Type I vs Type II error at foundation level?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Keep null/alternative and Type I/II in their standard directions. Regression fitting is a different topic; Type I and Type II are not the same event.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Null vs alternative; Type I = false reject; Type II = false retain; power = P(reject | H₁).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Swapping Type I/II, or displacing HT vocabulary into regression.

choices.label: The null and alternative frame the hypotheses under test. Type I error is rejecting a true null; Type II error is failing to reject a false null. Power is the probability of rejecting a false null.
Type I error is failing to reject a false null; Type II error is rejecting a true null.
Null and alternative matter only for linear regression fitting; they are not used in hypothesis testing vocabulary.
Type I and Type II errors are the same event whenever the p-value is below 5%.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.3.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Fraud flag: H₀ = genuine claim, H₁ = fraudulent. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Type I/II, p-value, power; refuse cookbook-as-concepts and regression.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: False fraud flag = Type I; missed fraud = Type II. Keep p-value and power in frequentist form. Neither software theatre nor regression fitting substitutes for the concepts.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Type I = false fraud flag; Type II = missed fraud; p-value under H₀; power = 1−β; refuse cookbook-as-concepts and regression conflation.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Swapping Type I/II, or treating a z-test click / regression fit as HT concepts.

choices.label: Type I: flag fraud when the claim is genuine. Type II: miss fraud when it is present. A p-value is the probability under H₀ of data at least as extreme as observed; power is P(reject H₀ | H₁ true). A software z-test click does not replace this vocabulary, and linear regression is a different topic.
Type I: miss fraud when present; Type II: flag fraud when genuine.
Because a software z-test can be run, Type I/II, p-value, and power definitions are optional.
HT foundations are the same skill as fitting a linear regression of loss on covariates.
